lessons_control.note: pre_lessons is each hunter's own sum before it read researcher_us/LESSONS.md. edge_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, which is the only thing that can tell the guidance file apart from a habit.

language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: US HRC spot kept climbing through Q3 and into Q4, after CLF set its Q3 guide on 23 July. Nucor CSP was $1,135/st on 20 Jul and $1,145/st on 27 Jul, then rose $10 a week to $1,190 (8 Sep), $1,220 (28 Sep), $1,230 (5 Oct) and $1,240 (12 Oct). SMU's HR assessment was $1,280/st for the week of 15 Oct, +$40 m/m, against $1,165/st on 21 Jul. Spot sits roughly $100+/st above the level the Q3 guide and the 'Q4 further exceeds Q3' language were set on, which points to a Q4 guide well above $575m and supports the ~$500m 2027 contract-reset uplift (2027 EBITDA up to $3.3bn per the July call).
findings.source_date: 2026-07-20 (page also carries the 2026-10-12 Nucor CSP $1,240/st and the SMU 15 Oct $1,280/st assessment)
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide line has driven the large moves: 2026-07-23 +15.98% (Q2 EPS miss, Q3 guide ~2x Q2); 2025-10-20 +21.47%; 2026-02-09 -16.43% on a weak outlook and slipped POSCO timing. The name pays heavily for guidance surprises in both directions.

findings.finding: The Q3 quarter is likely to land at or slightly above the $575m adjusted EBITDA guide. The guide assumed ASP +$55/t vs Q2's $1,124/t (about $1,179/t), unit cost -$10/t and shipments >4.3Mt, all set when spot was ~$1,135-1,165/st. Spot then rose through the quarter (Nucor CSP $1,160 on 10 Aug, $1,190 on 8 Sep, $1,220 on 28 Sep), and the spot/index-linked share of the book reprices with a 1-2 month lag, so realised price should come in at or above the guided uplift. Estimated beat about +2% on EBITDA, inside the 'approximately' range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Reported-quarter beats and misses have mattered less than the guide: Q2 2026 missed EPS (-$0.20 vs -$0.19) and rose 15.98% on the guide; Q1 2026 beat (narrower loss) and fell 2.11% on costs.

findings.finding: US natural gas was cheaper in Q3 than forecast: Henry Hub averaged about $2.78/MMBtu in August 2026 (FRED via MarketXLS), down from $2.89 in July and well below EIA's July STEO Q3 forecast of $3.37. That is a cost tailwind for an integrated BF/DRI steelmaker that took an $80m energy spike in Q1 2026, and supports the guided -$10/t unit cost.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Costs drove the Q1 2026 print: an $80m energy cost spike, and the stock fell 2.11% (reported 5%+ intraday) despite a beat.

findings.finding: Stelco (CLF's Canadian segment) is indefinitely idling Hamilton's cold-rolled and coated lines from 9 Oct, with 330-500 layoffs. Stelco's memo says demand for its cold-rolled and galvanized products fell almost 25% in Q2 2026 vs the 2024 quarterly average. Canada doubled its counter-tariff on US steel to 50% from 8 Sep, and the CEO said 'there's no market in Canada for the amount of galvanized steel we produce.' Ottawa (Carney, Joly) threatens legal action over the 2024 takeover commitments. Likely effects: Q4/2027 commentary on Stelco, idle costs, and a dent in the July claim that 'Stelco's improving performance' drives the $3.3bn 2027 figure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Canada has hurt before: the Feb 2026 print (-16.43%) cited a sluggish Canadian market. The stock fell to $11.3 in late August on a rumoured US-Canada tariff cut and rose 8% on 5 Oct as Canada-related pressure eased.

findings.finding: Stellantis, a major Detroit Three customer of CLF auto steel, reported Q3 2026 North American shipments down 12% y/y (-47k to 357k). Planned summer production pauses cut Jeep Grand Cherokee and Compass output by about 25k units each, partly offset by Ram (+17k). GM and Ford Q3 US sales fell 6% and 6.6%. CLF guided about half of its +300kt Q3 volume increase to come from automotive, and Q3 shipments of more than 4.3Mt.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Auto volume disappointment was part of the Feb 2026 -16.43% (the automotive market 'didn't provide a boost').

findings.finding: Steel Dynamics guided Q3 on 17 Sep (after CLF last spoke) with record steel shipments, rising realised prices and an order backlog nearly 50% above prior-year Q3, extending through Q1 2027. Nucor guided Q3 EPS to $5.55-5.65 vs $4.84 adjusted in Q2, with steel mills up on higher prices. This is order-book evidence that flat-rolled demand and pricing hold into Q4/Q1, which supports CLF's Q4 guide and its leverage in 2027 contract talks (non-auto talks conclude late Nov/early Dec).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: As the first finding: the guide line has moved this stock +16% to +21% and -16%.

findings.finding: The US-Canada steel tariff deal (50% to 25% on Canadian steel) that drove CLF's August sell-off to ~$11.3 did not happen. The US imposed Section 338 duties on Canadian goods from 22 Aug, Section 232 duties on Canadian steel stay at 50%, and Canada retaliated on 8 Sep. Import protection for CLF's US mills, the basis of management's pricing and 2027 reset thesis, is intact into the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Tariff headlines move this name: down to $11.3 on the rumoured cut (Aug 26 note), +8% on 5 Oct on tariff tailwinds.

findings.finding: No asset-sale or POSCO filing since the Q2 print. EDGAR for CIK 764065 shows only an 8-K item 5.02 (24 Jul), an SD, a 13G and Form 4s since 23 Jul. As of the July call only ~$100m of the ~$425m idled-property sale programme had been received, Toledo HBI offers fell 'short of our value threshold', and POSCO talks had 'made little progress' (the H1 2026 signing target was missed). Long-term debt rose to $7.70bn at 30 Jun from $7.25bn at year-end.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: POSCO timing slippage contributed to the 2026-02-09 -16.43% (shares fell more than 15% as the CEO pushed the timeline).

findings.finding: Positioning is crowded short into a guide-driven print: about 14.8-15.5% of float short (Benzinga ~Aug 10; MarketBeat undated), 84.5M shares at the last dated settlement (30 Apr, 3.67 DTC). The option market pays for upside (25d skew -15.8 vol pts, put/call OI 0.59), and the 5-day run-up is -5.23%. On a guide that is at least in line, short covering adds an upside mechanism; a weak guide meets shorts already positioned.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Positive guide prints gapped +15.98% (Jul 2026), +21.47% (Oct 2025) and +12.45% (Jul 2025), consistent with short covering amplifying up-moves.

outside_window.finding: 2027 non-automotive fixed-price contract negotiations typically conclude by late November/early December; their final reset level (vs ~$800/t prior-year basis and ~$1,150+ now) settles after the window. Only call commentary lands inside it.

findings.finding: Rates are now above what FITB's guide assumed. The July guide assumed one 25bp hike in September off the end-of-June forward curve. That hike came on 2026-09-16 (to 3.75-4.00%), and PNC's 2026-10-15 baseline now assumes two more (December 2026 and March 2027, to 4.25-4.50%). FITB disclosed year-two asset sensitivity of just under 10% plus fixed-rate asset repricing. PNC, on the same rate path, raised its FY26 NII outlook to about +15.5% (from 15-15.5%) and guided 4Q26 NII up about 4%. So a raised or firmed 4Q26/2027 NII outlook from FITB on 10-19 is more likely than the FY guide of $8.74-8.80bn implies.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Last print (2026-07-17) FITB raised its FY NII guide to $8.74-8.80bn, cut expense guidance and beat EPS ($1.02 against $0.98), and the stock fell 2.29%, so this name has recently sold a raise. Of the last seven prints, four were up, with a median absolute move of 1.31%.

findings.finding: Q3 AOCI and tangible book will take a hit from the long end. The 10-year went from about 4.4% in late June (4.41% on 06-24) to about 5.1-5.2% by late September and 5.24% on 10-09. FITB entered the quarter with AOCI of -$3.345bn, CET1 including AOCI of 8.7%, TCE including AOCI of 7.3%, TBV of $23.15, and $44.5bn of AFS securities. Peers who reported this week showed the size of it: PNC's AOCI went from -$4.1bn to -$6.5bn and TBV fell 3.1%, and Regions' TBV fell 8.2% ($13.78 to $12.65). A visible TBV decline and a lower AOCI-inclusive capital ratio raise the risk that the H2 buyback restart (guided as a smaller Q3, then $200-300m a quarter in Q4) is deferred or trimmed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nothing in the baseline isolates this line. In Q2 2026 the CET1 rise to 9.93% with no buybacks in H1 did not stop a -2.29% reaction.

findings.finding: Peers show commercial deposit pressure under rising rates. Regions' average deposits fell 1.2% q/q ($1.55bn), mainly as large corporate clients moved balances off balance sheet, and PNC's interest-bearing deposit rate rose 7bp to 1.98%. FITB's acquired Comerica franchise is heavily commercial and noninterest-bearing. On the Q2 call FITB said deposit costs would be 'stable to slightly up' and 'it certainly is getting more expensive to grow deposits'. That is a risk to Q4 NIM and to the deposit-mix commentary on 10-19.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 analysts pushed on deposit competition and beta (BofA, UBS, Goldman) and the stock fell 2.29% on the day, though the cause was not established.

findings.finding: The Comerica systems conversion (about 600k accounts and 293 branches, completed 2026-09-08) produced visible customer friction in Detroit and Dallas: account-access problems, crowded lobbies, long phone waits, the legacy app retired, bill-pay complaints, and a fraud warning. There is no evidence of deposit attrition or of a lasting outage after the first days.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior conversion print in the baseline.

findings.finding: Peer credit in Q3 2026 was benign to mixed, with no new NDFI or fraud event found in 2026. Regions' NCOs fell to 0.29% from 0.42%, its business criticized ratio fell to 4.71% from 5.01%, and its NPLs fell to 0.59%. PNC's NCOs were 0.28% (from 0.25%) with commercial NPLs up 8%. findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The October 2025 print (+1.31%) carried the roughly $178m Tricolor fraud loss and was still bought. FITB has absorbed a credit one-off before.

findings.finding: Fourth-quarter-to-date rates have reversed part of the September rout. The 10-year closed near 5.29% on Sept 30 (MND recap), peaked around 5.34% in early October, and was about 5.06-5.09% on Oct 15 after its biggest one-day rally in over a year. Freddie/MND 30-year mortgage rates fell from 7.49% (Oct 2) to 7.38% (Oct 14). If DX gives a quarter-to-date BV comment on the 10:00 call, it is more likely flat-to-up than down. However, MBS lagged Treasuries on Sept 30 and again on the Oct 15 rally day (UMBS 6.0 slightly down while the 10-year rallied), so the spread leg is not confirmed.

findings.finding: DX kept raising capital through the widening and deployed it into Agency MBS. It sold about 10M common shares between June 30 and July 24 (237.41M to 247.43M on the 10-Q cover), when the stock traded above the $12.90 BV, which is accretive. It then priced $120M of 9.375% Series D cumulative preferred on Sept 22 (closing Sept 29; ~$115.9M net, overallotment up to 720k more shares), explicitly to buy Agency and other securities. The preferred is non-dilutive to common BV and funds purchases at current-coupon spreads of about 120bp (BofA), which supports forward EAD and the case for an offensive posture on the call. The cost is a high fixed charge ahead of common.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: $391M raised and deployed, BV +2.4%, stock -1.58% on the print. Capital deployment has not been paid for on the print day.
